text:
Executive summary

This Place Delivery Agreement (PDA) is dated 17 November 2026 and strengthens the partnership between the West of England Combined Authority (WECA), Homes England and the National Housing Bank, creating an enhanced single delivery framework to accelerate housing delivery, help respond to affordability challenges across the region, unlock regeneration and strengthen economic growth across the West of England. While legislation for North Somerset joining the Combined Authority is awaited, for the purposes of this PDA, the West of England Combined Authority covers the unitary authorities of Bristol City, Bath and North East Somerset, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire Councils.

Building on the success of the Strategic Place Partnership, the Agreement represents a more ambitious approach to the way the 3 organisations work together. It moves beyond collaboration towards co-delivery of a set of shared priorities.

The Agreement is designed to support the Mayor’s ambitions for housing, regeneration and growth by bringing investment, delivery capability, specialist expertise and decision-making closer to place. Through this agreement, the partners commit to:

Priority 1: Delivering nationally significant growth and regeneration opportunities

Accelerating delivery of Bristol Temple Quarter and the West Innovation Arc.

Co-ordinating investment, infrastructure and delivery activity.

Driving the delivery of places that make the greatest contribution to the Mayor’s ambitions for housing, regeneration and growth.

Priority 2: Creating the next generation of growth opportunities

Supporting the development of the region’s Growth Zones and future strategic growth locations.

Strengthening long-term housing supply and infrastructure planning.

Creating a pipeline of opportunities which will deliver growth and prosperity in the future.

Priority 3: Creating a visible and investable housing and regeneration pipeline

Maintaining a shared pipeline of housing and regeneration opportunities across the region.

Improving project maturity, delivery readiness and investor confidence.

Accelerating the progression of opportunities from concept to delivery.

Giving the market greater confidence in the region’s long-term housing and regeneration pipeline.

Leading the nationally significant Small Sites Aggregator pathfinder, piloting new approaches to housing delivery on small public-sector sites and developing a model that could be scaled nationally.

Exploring innovative approaches to public sector land that maximise long-term public value while supporting housing delivery, including affordable housing, regeneration and economic growth.

Priority 4: Place-based investment and finance

Aligning Homes England and National Housing Bank activity with the Mayor’s priorities and regional growth ambitions.

Using the Future Places Fund, National Housing Bank and other investment mechanisms to unlock housing and regeneration opportunities.

Mobilising additional public, private and institutional capital into the delivery of housing, regeneration and infrastructure opportunities across the West of England.

Empowering WECA to shape housing investment and delivery priorities across all tenures.

Supporting mayoral influence over social and affordable housing investment decisions through regionally delegated Social and Affordable Housing Programme (SAHP) Continuous Market Engagement (CME) arrangements.

Priority 5: Accelerating affordable housing delivery and building the capacity and confidence required to deliver growth

Accelerating social, affordable and council housing delivery through improved co-ordination of the affordable housing pipeline and greater local influence over the Social and Affordable Homes Programme (SAHP) 2026 to 2036. This will help ensure investment aligns with the emerging Spatial Development Strategy and wider growth ambitions of the West of England.

Strengthening Registered Provider partnerships.

Addressing construction workforce and skills challenges.

Supporting SME builders, contractors and supply chains.

Building public sector delivery capability.

Creating the confidence required for employers, investors and delivery partners to invest in skills, supply chains and long-term housing growth.

Creating a dedicated Joint Delivery Unit

Establishing a Joint Delivery Unit (JDU) as a single delivery structure bringing together WECA, Homes England and National Housing Bank expertise.

Committing dedicated Homes England and National Housing Bank staff, including specialist expertise across:

partnerships

planning

regeneration

infrastructure

affordable housing

economics

development finance

legal services

market engagement

Providing a single route through which WECA can access the full range of Homes England and National Housing Bank delivery tools, expertise, investment capability and powers.

Aligning resources around shared priorities and accelerating the progression of projects from concept to delivery.

Strengthening accountability and governance

Creating significantly enhanced accountability through a shared performance framework and direct reporting arrangements to the Mayor.

Establishing strengthened oversight arrangements involving the Mayor, the Chairs of Homes England and the National Housing Bank, and the Chief Executives of both organisations.

Delegating day-to-day Homes England and National Housing Bank responsibility for delivery of the Agreement to the Homes England Executive Director for the South.

Nominated Co-Directors from both WECA and Homes England to lead the JDU.

Introducing quarterly senior sponsor meetings to oversee delivery, resolve barriers and hold the partnership to account for agreed outcomes.

Commencement and term

This PDA shall commence on the date of this agreement and shall continue for an initial period of 3 years (subject to an annual review) and shall thereafter continue for such further period or periods as shall be agreed in writing between the parties, provided always that any party may give not less than 90 days prior written notice to the others to terminate this PDA at any time.

This Agreement represents an enhanced model of place-based delivery. By combining local leadership, devolved influence, dedicated delivery capability, aligned investment and stronger accountability, WECA, Homes England and the National Housing Bank will work together to deliver more homes, unlock regeneration, attract investment and drive long-term economic growth across the West of England.

1. Place context and opportunity

1.1 The West of England is one of the UK’s most productive and innovative regions, combining internationally recognised cities, thriving market towns and rural communities, with globally significant strengths in advanced manufacturing, aerospace, creative industries, digital technologies, clean energy and higher education. Home to world-leading universities, internationally recognised businesses and a thriving innovation ecosystem, the region is uniquely positioned to contribute to national economic growth whilst delivering sustainable and inclusive local prosperity.

1.2 Through the West of England Growth Strategy, the Mayor and regional partners have set out a bold 10-year programme to drive economic transformation and improve quality of life across the region. Key ambitions include:

increasing regional GDP by 28%

creating 72,000 additional jobs

delivering approximately 7,750 new homes annually

increasing the proportion of journeys made by public transport and active travel

supporting the transition to a low-carbon economy

promoting growth that is inclusive, sustainable and benefits communities across the region

1.3 The West of England Mayoral Combined Authority works in partnership with the constituent authorities of Bath and North East Somerset, Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire. Together, these partners play a critical role in planning for growth, enabling development, delivering infrastructure and services, and bringing forward the housing and regeneration opportunities that will underpin the region’s long-term success.

1.4 Housing, social and affordable housing, infrastructure, skills, transport and economic development are increasingly interdependent. Delivering these ambitions will require co-ordinated investment, strong delivery capability and long-term partnership working between WECA, the constituent authorities, Homes England, the National Housing Bank and a wide range of public and private sector partners.

Strategic opportunities

1.5 The West of England contains nationally significant opportunities capable of increasing housing delivery, regeneration and economic growth over the coming decade. Major regeneration programmes, strategic growth locations and innovation-led development opportunities provide the foundation for a long-term programme of growth. These opportunities are supported by the region’s strengths in advanced manufacturing, research and development, clean energy, digital technologies and creative industries.

1.6 The region is also well positioned to benefit from investment in transport infrastructure, housing delivery and place-based regeneration, creating sustainable communities and supporting economic growth across both urban and rural areas.

1.7 Together, these opportunities provide the basis for a significant increase in housing delivery, productivity and investment, whilst supporting the Mayor’s ambitions for sustainable and inclusive growth.

Delivery challenges and market barriers

1.8 The challenge facing the West of England is not a lack of opportunity, but overcoming the barriers that prevent housing and regeneration projects progressing at the pace and scale required.

1.9 These barriers include infrastructure funding, development viability pressures, fragmented land ownership, capacity constraints within local authorities and limited access to long-term patient capital. The region also faces shortages across parts of the construction workforce, development professions and supply chain. These challenges are compounded where future development projects lack visibility, reducing confidence to invest in skills, recruitment, training and business growth.

1.10 Housing affordability is a fundamental constraint on inclusive growth across the West of England. High housing costs, constrained supply and insufficient delivery of homes affordable to local households are limiting access to secure housing, increasing pressure on temporary accommodation and affecting workforce recruitment and retention. Addressing this market failure requires a sustained increase in social and affordable housing alongside action to improve the affordability of the wider housing offer.

1.11 Many of these barriers are encountered across multiple projects and locations. As a result, opportunities that are strategically important to the region may not be delivered at the pace or scale required without co-ordinated intervention.

2. Going further, faster and rewiring the state

2.1 The SPP agreed in May 2025 has demonstrated the value of a co-ordinated approach, establishing a framework through which the Combined Authority and Homes England have aligned investment and delivery expertise around a number of the Mayor’s key priorities. This has included supporting delivery of Bristol Temple Quarter and the West Innovation Arc, progressing the Small Sites Aggregator as a nationally significant pathfinder, supporting development of the Future Places Fund and creating a shared prioritised housing and regeneration pipeline.

2.2 All partners now recognise we need to go much further, much faster, and show how we are rewiring the state to better serve the West of England. The PDA represents the next evolution of the Strategic Place Partnership, moving beyond collaboration towards co-delivery.

2.3 Together, the partners will establish a new model of place-based delivery capable of accelerating housing delivery, unlocking regeneration opportunities and supporting sustainable economic growth across the region. The JDU, operating under the strategic leadership of the Mayor and WECA, will provide a single delivery framework through which strategic ambition can be translated into investable propositions, faster decision-making and tangible delivery outcomes.

Place Delivery Agreement: A New Strategic Framework to Serve Places and Local Leaders

2.4 The PDA sets out a single framework through which WECA, Homes England and the National Housing Bank will align resources, expertise, capacity, investment and delivery activity to accelerate housing delivery, unlock regeneration opportunities and support the growth ambitions of the West of England.

2.5 The Agreement concentrates on a focused number of delivery priorities where a co-ordinated approach can have the greatest impact in overcoming barriers to delivery, attracting investment and bringing forward transformational housing and regeneration outcomes. These priorities reflect the shared ambition of both organisations to use housing, regeneration and place-based investment as a catalyst for economic growth, productivity and inclusive prosperity. More broadly, partners will maintain and enhance the existing WECA Housing Pipeline which will guide the deployment of resources, specialist support and investment activity across the region.

2.6 The priorities set out below will form the initial focus of activity under this Agreement. They will be reviewed periodically by the partners to ensure resources remain focused on the opportunities where joint intervention can deliver the greatest strategic impact.

2.7 Fundamentally, this framework is intended to ensure that local priorities, national and local capability and land, investment, powers and expertise are aligned around a common set of delivery objectives.

3. Theme A: Delivering large-scale transformation projects

Strategic priority 1: Delivering nationally significant growth and regeneration opportunities

3.1 The West of England contains some of the country’s most significant housing, regeneration and economic development opportunities. Delivering these opportunities is critical to achieving the region’s ambitions for housing delivery, productivity and sustainable economic growth.

3.2 Through the Place Delivery Agreement, partners will align delivery capability, investment and expertise around 2 transformational opportunities, Bristol Temple Quarter (BTQ) and the West Innovation Arc (WIA).

3.3 The partnership will seek to:

accelerate delivery of these transformational growth and regeneration programmes

co-ordinate infrastructure, investment and delivery activity

strengthen governance, commercial capability and delivery arrangements

ensure that major developments create lasting benefits for communities through new homes, jobs, investment and improved connectivity

3.4 Success will be measured through accelerated housing delivery, increased investment and the successful progression of BTQ and WIA.

Strategic priority 2: Creating the next iteration of growth opportunities

3.5 Delivering the scale of housing growth envisaged by the Mayor’s Growth Strategy requires a longer-term approach to place-making and spatial planning. Alongside progressing current opportunities, partners must also create the conditions for future housing and employment growth.

3.6 Through the Growth Zones programme and wider strategic planning activity, partners will work together to identify, shape and unlock future growth opportunities. Initial focus will include the Severn Estuary, Central Bath and Bristol, North Somerset Growth Gateway and Somer Valley.

3.7 The partnership will seek to:

strengthen the region’s long-term housing supply

improve infrastructure readiness and strategic planning

enable the development of sustainable and well-connected communities

identify future growth and investment opportunities

bring forward strategic growth opportunities aligned with transport, economic and environmental priorities

3.8 Success will be measured through the creation of a stronger long-term portfolio of growth opportunities capable of supporting housing delivery and economic growth for the future.

4. Theme B: Housing and regeneration pipeline

Strategic priority 3: Creating a viable and investable housing and regeneration pipeline

4.1 The West of England has a substantial number of housing and regeneration opportunities. However, many require further development, intervention or co-ordination before they can attract investment and progress to delivery.

4.2 Partners recognise that improving delivery is not solely about creating a stronger project pipeline. It is about creating confidence in the long-term development programme. Investors, developers, contractors, Registered Providers and training providers are all more likely to invest in capacity when they have greater certainty about future projects and programmes.

4.3 Through the Place Delivery Agreement, partners will maintain a shared regional housing and regeneration pipeline that supports prioritisation, informs investment decisions and provides greater visibility of future development opportunities.

Small Sites Aggregator

4.4 The West of England has been selected as a national pathfinder for the Small Sites Aggregator programme, a pioneering initiative designed to unlock the delivery of homes on small public-sector sites that are often overlooked by traditional development models. Through this innovative pilot, partners will work with local authorities, investors, SME housebuilders and delivery partners to test new approaches to site assembly, development finance and delivery. The programme has the potential to establish a scalable model that could inform future approaches to housing delivery across England, while accelerating affordable housing delivery within the West of England.

Strategic Public Land

4.5 The partners will explore whether there is potential to unlock greater social and economic value from public sector land across the West of England. This could test a more co-ordinated approach to identifying, assembling and unlocking public land opportunities across the region. Through the JDU, working with wider public sector partners, the partners will explore whether a pipeline of priority sites could be identified, explore barriers to delivery, and assess the potential for a longer-term public sector land programme that could accelerate housing delivery (including affordable housing), regeneration and economic growth.

4.6 The partnership will seek to:

maintain a shared housing and regeneration pipeline

improve project maturity and delivery readiness

accelerate project development and business case preparation

prioritise opportunities where co-ordinated intervention can unlock delivery

increase visibility of future development opportunities across the region and improve market engagement and investor confidence

support the delivery and evaluation of the Small Sites Aggregator pathfinder programme, developing a scalable model for unlocking smaller public-sector sites and informing future approaches to housing delivery across England

explore innovative approaches to public sector land that could unlock housing delivery, regeneration and economic growth while maximising long-term public value

4.7 A visible and investable pipeline will help bring forward projects more quickly, create greater confidence amongst investors and developers, and provide the certainty needed for employers, supply chains and training providers to invest in future workforce capacity.

4.8 Success will be measured through a growing pipeline of mature, investable projects progressing towards delivery, the development of opportunities aligned to National Housing Bank products, Future Places Fund interventions and wider investment mechanisms, and the development and testing of innovative approaches capable of accelerating housing and regeneration outcomes.

5. Theme C: Shared thematic priorities

5.1 The partners recognise that achieving the scale of change envisaged through the Local Growth Plan requires more than investment alone. It requires greater alignment between local priorities, national capability and investment decision-making. Through this Agreement, Homes England and the National Housing Bank will support WECA to create a more integrated and locally responsive system, ensuring that the full range of housing, regeneration and growth interventions are aligned behind the Mayor’s priorities.

5.2 This PDA represents an opportunity to bring decision-making, delivery capability and investment capability closer to place. The PDA will strengthen the region’s influence over key elements of the housing and regeneration system, enabling local priorities to shape the deployment of funding, specialist expertise and delivery support.

5.3 The thematic priorities set out below focus on those areas where greater local influence, co-ordinated action and aligned investment can have the greatest impact on housing delivery, regeneration outcomes and economic growth. Together, they will help create the conditions required to unlock a stronger pipeline of housing and regeneration opportunities and support the delivery of the region’s long-term ambitions.

5.4 Through this PDA, partners will seek to strengthen local influence over housing investment, delivery capability and the deployment of specialist expertise, enabling local priorities to shape interventions more directly.

Strategic priority 4: Place-based investment and finance

5.5 The delivery of the West of England’s housing and regeneration ambitions will require investment at a scale that cannot be achieved through grant funding alone. Unlocking transformational opportunities across the region will depend on the ability to combine public and private capital, recycle investment over time and develop investable propositions capable of attracting long-term institutional funding.

5.6 The National Housing Bank, launched by Homes England in 2026, has been established to accelerate the delivery of new homes and mixed-use regeneration schemes through flexible public investment. Backed by up to £16 billion of debt, equity and guarantee products, the Bank is designed to work with national, regional and local partners to unlock housing delivery, crowd-in private capital and support the government’s ambition to deliver 1.5 million homes, whilst delivering a positive financial return for the Exchequer.

5.7 WECA and Homes England share an ambition to use the PDA as a platform to develop innovative approaches to place-based investment, enhancing the existing WECA Housing Pipeline of investable housing and regeneration opportunities and increasing the scale of private capital investment into the Region. Through the Future Places Fund, National Housing Bank and wider investment activity, partners will work together to align funding, finance and investment expertise around regional priorities, ensuring that projects are able to access the support required to progress.

5.8 As part of this Agreement, the National Housing Bank will actively seek opportunities to amplify the region’s Future Places Fund, and will explore opportunities to potentially invest up to £250 million in suitable housing pipeline projects, to support housing and regeneration ambitions and the Mayor’s priorities to attract wider investment using its lending, equity or guarantee capacity.

5.9 The National Housing Bank will support the development of a portfolio of investment opportunities capable of unlocking a significantly greater level of private and institutional capital investment over time, including from the National Housing Bank.

5.10 Partners will work together to identify and develop housing-led regeneration, infrastructure-enabled growth, mixed-use development and strategic land opportunities that have the potential to unlock significantly greater levels of private and institutional investment over time.

5.11 The partnership will seek to:

maintain and enhance the prioritised pipeline of investable housing and regeneration opportunities across the West of England

align National Housing Bank products and investment capabilities with the Future Places Fund and mayoral growth and regeneration priorities

explore opportunities to deploy National Housing Bank products alongside the Future Places Fund, institutional capital and private investment to accelerate delivery of priority projects.

maximise investment into the region through targeted promotion, advice and support to public and private sector partners

explore innovative approaches to land, infrastructure and development finance that improve viability and accelerate delivery

develop scalable and replicable investment models that can be applied across a wider pipeline of housing and regeneration opportunities

5.12 Success will be measured through increased investment into housing, regeneration and infrastructure projects across the West of England.

Strategic priority 5: Accelerating affordable housing delivery and building the capacity and confidence required to deliver growth

5.13 Delivering the region’s housing ambitions will require more than land, planning permissions and investment. It will require the workforce, institutions, partnerships and supply chains capable of sustaining delivery over the long term.

5.14 Partners increasingly recognise that affordable housing delivery, construction skills, public sector capability and market confidence are interconnected challenges that influence the pace and scale of housing delivery. Addressing these challenges will be fundamental to achieving the region’s growth ambitions.

5.15 This priority focuses on strengthening the housing delivery system that sits behind growth.

Social and Affordable housing and council housebuilding delivery

5.16 Affordable housing is one of the clearest examples of how this PDA will bring decision-making, delivery capability and accountability closer to place.

5.17 WECA’s recent designation as an Established Mayoral Strategic Authority will enable the authority to play a more influential role in shaping affordable housing delivery across the region. Through this Agreement, the JDU will ensure affordable housing investment is aligned with the Mayor’s priorities for growth, regeneration and housing delivery. By combining regional decision-making with dedicated delivery capability and specialist affordable housing expertise, the partnership will enable investment decisions to be shaped more directly by local priorities and delivery opportunities.

5.18 The partnership will take a phased approach to WECA’s involvement in affordable housing investment and programme activity, in recognition of the time required to develop the capability and supporting arrangements needed to assume this enhanced role. The Local Housing Needs Assessment (LHNA), Spatial Development Strategy (SDS) and related evidence work will help establish a clearer understanding of housing need, affordability pressures and future delivery priorities across the region, providing the foundation for future investment and delivery decisions.

5.19 Initial activity will focus on:

using the LHNA to strengthen the evidence base for affordable housing need

embedding affordable housing considerations within broader pipeline decision-making

improving co-ordination with Registered Providers to develop a coherent regional approach to increase investment in affordable housing

5.20 As part of this full enhanced role, the partnership will ensure activity and investment are directed towards opportunities that can unlock or accelerate delivery, address housing need and contribute to the ambitions of the Local Growth Plan. This will include:

SAHP decisions on Continuous Market Engagement (CME) will be delegated to the Regional SAHP team (within agreed thresholds) with the JDU providing the governance forum for approval, to enable investment decisions to be locally led and determined

the Mayor and WECA will be given full visibility of the affordable housing pipeline data in their area. Through the JDU and enhanced governance they will be included in the affordable housing pipeline review and CME assessment process providing local insights and data to develop proposals

the Mayor and WECA will be involved in the assessment and decision-making process for further procurement rounds or extensions to existing Strategic Partnership allocations that affect the region

a clearly defined escalation process if members of the JDU cannot agree on the SAHP CME investment decision to be made, via the PDA, JDU or respective governance structures for a definitive decision — this will be through monthly governance

working with Registered Provider Strategic Partners operating within the SAHP to align investment plans and develop a co-ordinated pipeline of social and affordable housing opportunities across the region, supporting delivery of the Mayor’s affordable housing and regeneration priorities

5.21 Recognising the government’s ambition to significantly increase council house delivery, Homes England will support the WECA to:

review the barriers to delivery of council housing and work collaboratively with local authorities to implement the preferred approaches including the potential to align with other thematic areas including land, industrialised construction and other forms of investment

bring empty homes back into use and other improvements to existing stock including where there are positive links to be made to other policy areas such as reduced use of temporary accommodation

Local Housing Systems Analysis Pathfinder

5.22 The partners will work together to progress the West of England as a Pathfinder for the Local Housing Systems Analysis programme, developing a shared evidence base to better understand housing market dynamics, delivery constraints and opportunities across the region. This work will support evidence-led decision making, inform investment and intervention priorities, strengthen local capability and help identify the actions required to accelerate housing delivery and improve housing outcomes. The outputs will be used to underpin future strategic planning, investment decisions and delivery programmes across the West of England.

Public sector delivery capability

5.23 The partnership will strengthen planning, regeneration, technical and programme management capability across the region by identifying and diagnosing barriers to delivery and co-ordinating targeted support to address them. This may include convening relevant organisations and expertise, facilitating peer learning and best practice, and working with partners to develop solutions to common challenges. For example, the partnership may support collaborative workshops, technical assistance and knowledge-sharing activities to help address issues such as planning capacity, infrastructure co-ordination and project delivery.

Construction skills and market capacity

5.24 Delivering housing growth at scale will require significant increases in workforce capacity across both construction and development professions.

5.25 Partners will work with employers, colleges, universities, training providers and industry bodies to strengthen workforce planning, support apprenticeship pathways and improve employer engagement in skills development.

5.26 The partnership will also work to attract additional delivery capacity into the region, recognising the important role that skilled labour, supply chains and specialist expertise play in sustaining housing delivery at scale.

5.27 The partnership will seek to:

strengthen construction skills provision and workforce planning

support SME builders and contractors

improve engagement between employers and training providers

attract additional delivery capacity into the region

promote long-term confidence in future housing and regeneration programmes

5.28 Together these interventions will help create a stronger housing delivery system for the West of England. Success will be measured through the strength of the housing delivery system that underpins growth, including a more investable project pipeline, increased social, affordable and council housing delivery, a stronger and more visible affordable housing pipeline, stronger public sector capability, better evidence to inform decision-making, greater market confidence and a workforce equipped to support long-term housing and regeneration delivery.

5.29 These priorities reflect a shared commitment to delivering the Mayor’s ambitions for housing, regeneration and economic growth. By aligning around a focused set of place-based priorities, the partnership will work to unlock opportunities, address barriers to delivery and build the conditions required for long-term growth across the region.

6. Next steps: Delivery, governance and implementation

6.1 This new single framework will help to strengthen local capability to support delivery, while recognising a desire to go further in boosting the capacity, expertise and sharing of good practice across the public and private sector partners in the sub-region via a focused programme of activity.

6.2 The JDU will provide greater visibility and accountability to the Mayor, giving the Mayor the control, influence and resources needed to build the homes and places communities require and to hold partners to account for delivery.

6.3 WECA, Homes England and the National Housing Bank commit to progressing a joint delivery plan outlining key tasks, milestones and resourcing commitments underpinned by a governance framework that delivers the principles outlined in this PDA.

6.4 Successful delivery of the PDA will require close collaboration with the constituent authorities of Bath and North East Somerset, Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire. The JDU will work with local authority partners to identify opportunities, address barriers to delivery, develop the shared pipeline of housing and regeneration opportunities and ensure local priorities are reflected in delivery planning and investment decisions.

Partnership commitments

6.5 The parties commit to:

align resources around mayoral priorities

maintain and enhance the West of England’s shared strategic development and investment pipeline, developed and prioritised in partnership with the constituent Local Authorities

jointly identify and resolve barriers

co-ordinate stakeholder engagement

share intelligence and investment planning

support delivery through a dedicated JDU

6.6 This PDA will operate on a 3-year basis and will be reviewed annually to ensure it remains aligned with evolving national policy, mayoral priorities, market conditions and delivery opportunities. The PDA is intended to provide a single framework while retaining sufficient flexibility to respond to changing circumstances and emerging priorities.

6.7 Delivery of the PDA will be supported through:

a rolling delivery programme maintained through the JDU, responding to mayoral priorities, interventions and opportunities requiring joint action

a detailed annual Delivery Plan, agreed following approval of the PDA, translating strategic priorities into specific actions, responsibilities, milestones and resource commitments

an annual review process to refresh delivery priorities, resource allocations and pipeline activity without requiring the full PDA to be renegotiated

regular monitoring and performance reporting through the governance and accountability arrangements within this PDA, enabling partners to track progress, identify emerging risks and agree corrective action where required

6.8 The parties acknowledge that successful delivery will require ongoing collaboration between Homes England, the National Housing Bank, WECA and wider delivery partners, including local authorities, government departments, infrastructure providers, registered providers, investors and other stakeholders.

Joint Delivery Unit

6.9 The PDA is delivered through a Joint Delivery Unit (JDU), which acts as the single delivery interface between WECA, Homes England and the National Housing Bank. The JDU provides the resource, expertise and co-ordination needed to progress agreed priorities and projects, drawing on specialist capability from across Homes England and the National Housing Bank where required. Strategic direction is provided through the PDA governance arrangements, with priorities, resources and performance reviewed through an agreed Delivery Plan.

6.10 The JDU will support delivery through the following functions:

programme management

opportunity identification

pipeline development

major project delivery

investment co-ordination

risk management

performance monitoring

6.11 The capacities and capabilities set out below have informed development of this Agreement and represent indicative Day 1 commitments. The resources identified below will be recruited and employed by Homes England and made available to support delivery of the shared priorities agreed under this PDA. These staff will remain within Homes England’s management and accountability arrangements and will work closely with WECA colleagues, who will continue to operate within WECA’s own management and accountability structures. The allocation of resources, agreement of operational priorities and co-ordination of delivery activity will be determined jointly through the Delivery Plan and associated governance arrangements. These arrangements do not constitute the secondment or transfer of staff between organisations.

Core capabilities

Senior leadership and accountability — Leadership and sponsorship of Place Delivery Agreements within Homes England. Provides the strategic interface between local leaders and the Agency, aligning national priorities with local ambitions, resolving barriers to delivery, and ensuring places can rapidly access the full breadth of agency capabilities.

Partnership management and co-ordination (including diagnostics and skills commissioning) — Day-to-day partnership leadership. Develops strategic priorities with WECA, co-ordinates development and delivery of associated delivery plans and pipelines, undertakes diagnostics, facilitates relationship brokerage between public and private sector partners (including different parts of government) and leads relevant workstreams as required.

Delivery support — Day-to-day working level support for the above activities.

Social and Affordable Homes Programme interface — Responsible for co-ordinating affordable housing investment via SAHP in the WECA area.

National Housing Bank interface — Responsible for co-ordinating National Housing Bank activity in the WECA area, including alignment with the Future Places Fund and other place-based investment initiatives where appropriate.

Project-specific delivery resources

Project Director — West Innovation Arc and BTQ

Head — West Innovation Arc

Head — BTQ

Senior Manager — BTQ

Senior Manager — Small Sites Aggregator

Senior Manager — Growth Zones

Pipeline and thematic priorities

6.12 Specific pipeline, programme and thematic priorities will be agreed through development of the Delivery Plan. This will include identification of priority projects, workstreams, outcomes and resource requirements.

6.13 The JDU will be complemented by housing delivery expertise from across the wider Agency shaped to develop products, schemes and initiatives as part of this thematic capability, including on:

social and affordable housing

National Housing Bank finance and product specialists

specialist technical capabilities

strategy, research and innovation capacity

6.14 The specialist capabilities available to support the JDU are expected initially to include:

Affordable Housing Grants

Advisory Team for Large Applications (ATLAS) — specialist planning support

climate, environment and sustainability

commercial strategy

communications

community engagement and social impact

Compulsory Purchase Order

contingent assets and liabilities

design, masterplanning and placemaking

development finance (National Housing Bank)

disposals

economics

equity and partnerships (National Housing Bank)

estates

geospatial

Guarantees (National Housing Bank)

Infrastructure Grants Project Management

Infrastructure Loans (National Housing Bank)

Low Interest Loans (National Housing Bank)

New Homes Accelerator (specialist delivery unblocking)

planning and enabling

risk

strategic development and delivery

strategic planning

strategy, research and analysis and market engagement

structured real estate finance (National Housing Bank)

technical services

Governance and accountability

6.15 The Governance Framework will be developed further through the Delivery Plan and will include:

creating significantly enhanced accountability through a shared performance framework and direct reporting arrangements to the Mayor

establishing strengthened oversight arrangements involving the Mayor, the Chairs of Homes England and the National Housing Bank, and the Chief Executives of both organisations

introducing quarterly senior sponsor meetings to oversee delivery, resolve barriers and hold the partnership to account for agreed outcomes

6.16 In recognition of the commitment to create an even more responsive and re-wired delivery body as outlined in the Housing Minister’s letter, and to bring decision-making and accountability closer to impacted communities, the parties will commit in parallel to review existing delegations, reporting and accountability frameworks. Communications and stakeholder engagement activity will similarly be reviewed to maximise Homes England impact. Homes England will ensure information on planned activity within the geographical area of the WECA will be shared with WECA in advance via the JDU.

Delivery Plan

6.17 The PDA will be supported by a detailed Delivery Plan which will provide the primary mechanism for co-ordinating delivery activity and monitoring progress against agreed commitments.

6.18 The Delivery Plan will:

translate the strategic priorities and commitments set out within this PDA into deliverable programmes, projects and interventions

set out key milestones, outputs, funding requirements, resource commitments and critical dependencies

identify risks, constraints and barriers to delivery, together with proposed mitigation measures and required decisions

establish performance measures, success indicators and reporting arrangements

maintain a forward pipeline of opportunities and activities to support delivery of shared priorities

identify areas where additional collaboration, investment or intervention may be required to achieve agreed outcomes

Each partnership commitment included within the Delivery Plan will identify:

a named lead owner

target completion or review dates

expected outputs and outcomes

success measures and monitoring arrangements

6.19 Following approval of the PDA, the JDU will co-ordinate preparation of the Delivery Plan and maintain it as a live document throughout the life of the PDA.

The partners will agree:

the timetable for preparation and implementation of the Delivery Plan

the lead organisation responsible for co-ordinating drafting and updates

governance arrangements for review, endorsement and approval

the senior officers authorised to approve revisions and updates

reporting arrangements to support effective oversight and accountability

6.20 The JDU will co-ordinate preparation of the Delivery Plan and maintain it as a live document throughout the life of the PDA.

Annual review

6.21 The PDA will be subject to an annual review led by the JDU and overseen through the governance arrangements referred to in this PDA. It will report to the Mayor, the Chief Executive of the Combined Authority, the Chief Executive of Homes England and the Chair of Homes England.

The review will:

assess progress against the commitments and success measures set out in the Delivery Plan

consider emerging opportunities, risks and policy developments

review resource requirements and delivery capacity

refresh the rolling programme of activity and priority projects

recommend amendments to the Delivery Plan where required

6.22 Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, changes arising through the annual review process will be managed through updates to the Delivery Plan and will not require the PDA itself to be redrafted or re-executed.

6.23 This approach will ensure that the PDA remains a stable long-term framework while enabling partners to adapt delivery activity in response to changing circumstances and opportunities.
